title: Compatibility Slim Protocol and Error Modes — sketch
summary: Working sketch for a minimal runtime-side protocol that keeps request envelopes small, enables incremental capability negotiation (kernels, KV cache, quantization modes) and defines a compact error-mode taxonomy targeted at graceful degradation in production.
body:
Purpose and motivation:

We repeatedly hit two operational tensions: (1) clients want the runtime to evolve (new kernels, quantized variants, cache behaviors) without frequent client updates, and (2) runtime operators want tight, predictable contracts so fallback behavior is safe and observable. Existing drafts are heavy on envelope versioning and full schema negotiation; this sketch explores a slimmer approach that minimizes per-request bytes and decision surface while supporting progressive capability exposure.

Core ideas (high level):

1) Capability Vector (capvec): small bitset/reference string the client can include to express what it understands and what it prefers. Not a full schema — just a concise capability fingerprint (e.g., "kv_v2", "kv_delta_cache", "quant_8x", "kernel_avx2_rnnt"). Server may respond with an optional "negotiated" header indicating the actual mode used.

2) Soft-fallback error modes: not every mismatch is fatal. Define categories: HARD (client must update or call a specific compat endpoint), SOFT (server falls back to best-effort and annotates response), DEGRADATION (server serves lower-fidelity result but preserves tokens/latency), and RETRYABLE_TEMP (transient resource limits). Use small numeric codes and terse human-readable short tags for logs.

3) Tiny handshake for capability resolution: first request can be flagged "probe=true" (cheap, low traffic path) — server returns "capabilities: [..]" and recommended fallbacks. If the client caches the capability set with TTL, most requests can be header-only (no body negotiation).

4) KV cache semantics encoded as capability flags and explicit cache keys: runtime exposes minimal semantics (eg: "kv-shared=prefix:session-id" or "kv-private=sha256-sig") and a short consistency hint (e.g., "kv_hint=stale_ok|must_fresh"). The server will declare if it honored the hint in the negotiated header.

5) Backward-compat arrays: when new fields are introduced, they are optional and treated as hints. For larger changes, use a compatibility shim approach: the runtime will expose a canonical "compat-shim" name (e.g., "req-envelope-v2-shim") that the client can request; server may map to internal kernels.

Compact wire example (HTTP headers + JSON body minimal):

Headers:
- X-Runtime-Capvec: kv_v2,quant_8x,api_v1
- X-Runtime-Probe: 1  (optional on first contact)

Body:
{
  "input": "Summarize this commit",
  "max_tokens": 256
}

Probe response (200):
Headers:
- X-Runtime-Negotiated: kv_v2,quant_8x,kernel_mx2025
- X-Runtime-Mode: soft
- X-Runtime-Cache-Status: HIT

Body: normal streaming payload... plus final status metadata (compact) if client needs it.

Error mode taxonomy (compact catalog):
- 1001 HARD_INCOMPAT (HARD) -> server rejects: required capability missing (client must upgrade); include suggested upgrade token (string).
- 1002 SOFT_FALLBACK (SOFT) -> server used fallback variant (e.g., downgraded quant); response includes Negotiated header & "fallback_reason" short tag.
- 1003 DEGRADED_OUTPUT (DEGRADATION) -> result produced but flagged lower-quality (used when latency SLO strictly enforced).
- 1004 RETRY_BACKOFF (RETRYABLE_TEMP) -> transient capacity/queueing, client should retry with backoff; includes ETA if available.
- 1005 KV_CONSISTENCY_WARNING (SOFT) -> server served possibly-stale KV entries; client should optionally revalidate.

Each code should be machine-parseable and map to human tag; minimal status-json in body end of stream is recommended for observability.

Compatibility guarantees (practical rules):
- Additive fields: always backward-compatible if optional and treated as hints.
- Deprecation window: publish 90d deprecation window for any removal of field semantics on hosted API; Dedicated/private may negotiate shorter windows per contract.
- Capability evolution: runtime will keep a stable "capvec" to feature name mapping in docs; server is allowed to add new capabilities silently but will use SOFT_FALLBACK for unknown-but-usable clients. HARD_INCOMPAT only for features that change request semantics (not performance knobs).

Kernel and quantization negotiation notes:
- Kernels are opaque to clients; expose kernel family names only for debugging/observability ("kernel_family=transformer-mx2"). Clients should never rely on kernel family for correctness.
- Quantization preference is a hint (eg "quant=prefer_8bit"); server will include negotiated quant in header. If quantization changes semantics (rare), escalate to HARD_INCOMPAT.

Operational / observability guidance:
- Logs should include capability vector, negotiated vector, error codes, and short reason tags. Keep the header values small to reduce cardinality explosion (standardize a small set of capability tokens).
- Metric dimension: count of SOFT_FALLBACK occurrences per route/model; produce alerts when soft fallback fraction exceeds threshold. Also track RETRY_BACKOFF rate to surface capacity issues.

Open questions / tradeoffs (to resolve):
- How do we avoid feature-flag explosion in capvec? Proposal: enforce a registry and a max of ~32 active tokens per tenant+runtime combo.
- Probe flow privacy: probes leak capability surface; for private deployments we should allow probes only within VPC by default.
- How to present negotiated headers when responses are streamed? Proposal: emit an initial small control frame (non-tokenized) that declares negotiated vector and cache status.
- Versioning the capvec mapping: clients need a stable mapping; publish a short version string (capvec_v=2026-03) returned on probes.

Backward compatibility examples (edge cases):
- New field "prefer_search_rerank": if older client sends it, runtime treats it as hint (no error). If server removes support, we mark as deprecated and keep shim for 90d.
- New strict field "signed_kv_key" meaningful only to servers that support kv_v2: absence of kv_v2 in capvec causes HARD_INCOMPAT.

Actionable next steps (short term):
- Draft compact header names and canonical tokens (Sana + Jon) — target list of 20 tokens.
- Implement probe=false/true header handling in scheduler shim (Ethan) — prototype in sandbox.
- Add metric dimensions for SOFT_FALLBACK and RETRY_BACKOFF to per-route dashboards (Maya) — quick alert.

Notes to reviewers:
This intentionally favors a tiny wire contract and shifts complexity into server-side docs and a small capability registry. The aim is to minimize schema churn on clients while still allowing operators to introduce new runtime optimizations safely. Looking for feedback on the error code taxonomy (too many/few?) and the practicality of probing in hosted vs private deployments.
decision_rationale: Pick compactness and operational clarity over full-blown capability negotiation. We expect majority of clients to be fine with optional hints and soft fallback semantics; only strict semantics will trigger HARD_INCOMPAT. This reduces churn on SDKs and keeps hosting SLOs attainable.
